posts.text: On this day in 1964, America moved toward realizing the promise of equal justice under law. Passage of the Civil Rights Act after Freedom Summer and the deaths of Schwerner, Chaney and Goodman, reminds us that every hard-won right has come through courage, collective action and a passionate belief in democratic change. Today, it’s our turn to fight back in the face of rampant authoritarianism to guard the rights and liberties of our people.

President Trump’s quest to destroy birthright citizenship has failed. The president’s executive order was a direct and blatant violation of the first sentence of the Fourteenth Amendment, as numerous district and appeals court judges ruled. Today, a narrow majority of the Supreme Court, including one justice nominated by Trump himself (Barrett), rejected the President’s blood-and-soil attempt to deny a huge number of children born in America their equal constitutional birthright.


The Associate

posts.text: We hold the power of the purse and a Congressional appropriation is a federal law. Thus the president must take care to faithfully execute all budget appropriations. Trump has violated the Constitution by shutting down USAID and now withholding $19 billion in congressionally appropriated foreign aid. His refusal to write the checks for USAID’s lifesaving global programs against malaria, HIV/AIDS and hunger is a deadly form of law-breaking.
